The resolver portion is correct, but the guard blocker is not fully closed. I found two medium issues in the uncommitted response to the [review comment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2241#issuecomment-5511224983).

Reviewing `refactor-git-metadata-owner` vs `upstream/main`: 2 commits, 7 files.  
Current response: 3 uncommitted files, +355/−151.  
Intent context: 2 Entire checkpoints plus the linked review comment.

## metadata_guard_test.go

Medium: Metadata-query exceptions are function-wide rather than flag-specific.

At [metadata_guard_test.go:116](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/refactor-git-metadata-owner/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go:116), detecting any of the four flags checks only whether the function is allowlisted. For example, `dispatch_wizard.go:resolveGitTopLevel` is allowed for `--show-toplevel`; adding `--git-dir` to that same function would also pass silently.

This means the guard detects the newly named flags in new functions, but does not maintain an exact inventory inside existing exceptions.

Fix: key `allowedMetadataQueries` and `metadataQueriesSeen` by both function and flag, such as `{sourceKey, flag}`.

Medium: The new tests exercise detector helpers rather than the complete source-scanning contract.

[metadata_guard_test.go:169](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/refactor-git-metadata-owner/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go:169) parses a single synthetic file and calls the value resolver directly. It therefore does not prove that cross-file package constants flow through `collectGuardPackageStringValues`.

Likewise, [metadata_guard_test.go:278](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/refactor-git-metadata-owner/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go:278) only checks `isGuardSourceFile("internal/probe/probe.go")`. Reverting the actual walker to `cmd/entire/cli` while leaving that predicate unchanged would keep the test green.

Fix: extract the complete scan into a function accepting a repository root. Run it against a temporary miniature repository containing:

- a package constant in one file and its forbidden use in another;
- a forbidden source under `internal/`;
- the shadowed `gitDir` parameter as a negative control.

Low: The PR description overstates and omits verification details.

The current [PR description](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2241) says positive controls prove `Readlink`, but the current test table contains no `Readlink` case. It also does not include the reviewer’s requested measurable result: 7/7 pointer spellings now agree with Git versus 3/7 before.

Fix: restore a `Readlink` positive control and add the before/after result to the description.

## Cleared

The rest of the comment is addressed:

- Package-level metadata tokens are followed.
- `--absolute-git-dir`, `--git-dir`, `--show-toplevel`, and `--git-common-dir` are inspected.
- `OpenRoot` is included.
- Production scanning starts at the repository root.
- An unrelated `gitDir` parameter is no longer treated as `.git`.
- [ResolveWorktreeMetadata("")](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/refactor-git-metadata-owner/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_test.go:227) enters through the real resolver seam.
- The additional symlink-containment change fails closed through both `ResolveWorktreeMetadata` and `OpenPath`.

System model: this change performs no writes. `ResolveWorktreeMetadata` owns reads; the guard owns source-policy enforcement. Interruption cannot leave partial durable state, and retry requires no cleanup.

Verification completed:

- Focused reviewer-response tests: passed.
- Full `gitrepo` package: passed.
- `gofmt` check: clean.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Found 3 issues: 0 critical, 0 high, 2 medium, 1 low. I would tighten the guard and its production-seam tests before calling the review comment fully resolved.
I’ll turn the completed audit into a root-level `review.md`, preserving the scope, findings, system model, cleared checks, and verification evidence.

+# Correctness Review: PR #2241 Review Response
+
+Review target: the uncommitted response to [PR #2241 review comment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2241#issuecomment-5511224983).
+
+## Conclusion
+
+The resolver portion is correct, but the guard blocker is not fully closed. The response addresses the reviewer’s named detection cases, yet the guard still has a function-wide exception gap and its new tests do not exercise the complete repository-scanning seam.
+
+Found three issues: zero critical, zero high, two medium, and one low.
+
+## Scope
+
+- Branch: `refactor-git-metadata-owner`
+- Base: `upstream/main`
+- Branch diff: two commits, seven files
+- Uncommitted review response: three files, 355 insertions and 151 deletions
+- Intent context: two Entire checkpoints, the linked review comment, and the current PR description
+
+Files in the uncommitted response:
+
+- `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go`
+- `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_test.go`
+
+## Findings
+
+### `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/metadata_guard_test.go`
+
+#### Medium: Metadata-query exceptions are function-wide rather than flag-specific
+
+At line 116, detecting any of these flags checks only whether the containing function is allowlisted:
+
+- `--absolute-git-dir`
+- `--git-common-dir`
+- `--git-dir`
+- `--show-toplevel`
+
+For example, `dispatch_wizard.go:resolveGitTopLevel` is allowlisted for `--show-toplevel`. Adding `--git-dir` to the same function would also pass silently because `allowedMetadataQueries` and `metadataQueriesSeen` are keyed only by function.
+
+This detects the newly named flags in new functions, but it does not maintain an exact inventory inside existing exceptions.
+
+Recommended fix: key both maps by function and flag, for example with a `{sourceKey, flag}` struct.
+
+#### Medium: The tests exercise detector helpers instead of the complete source scan
+
+`TestGitMetadataGuardRecognizesBypassForms`, starting at line 169, parses one synthetic file and invokes the value resolver directly. It does not prove that a constant declared in one file reaches a forbidden use in another through `collectGuardPackageStringValues`.
+
+`TestGitMetadataGuardScansProductionOutsideCLI`, starting at line 278, checks only this predicate:
+
+```go
+isGuardSourceFile("internal/probe/probe.go")
+```
+
+If the actual walker were changed back to `cmd/entire/cli` while this predicate remained unchanged, the test would stay green and a production parser under `internal/` would again bypass the guard.
+
+Recommended fix: extract the complete scan into a function that accepts a repository root, then run it against a temporary miniature repository containing:
+
+- a package constant in one file and a forbidden use in another;
+- a forbidden source under `internal/`;
+- a shadowed `gitDir` parameter as a negative control.
+
+This would enter through the same walker, package-value collection, value resolution, and policy reporting used by the real guard.
+
+#### Low: The PR description overstates and omits verification details
+
+The [PR description](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2241) says positive controls prove `Readlink`, but the current bypass-test table has no `Readlink` case. The description also does not include the reviewer’s requested measurable result: the parser now agrees with Git on seven of seven pointer spellings, compared with three of seven before the refactor.
+
+Recommended fix: restore a `Readlink` positive control and add the before-and-after pointer-spelling result to the PR description.
+
+## Review Comment Correspondence
+
+| Review point | Status | Evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Detect package-level metadata-token constants | Addressed in implementation; integration proof is incomplete | `collectGuardPackageStringValues` and `guardValueResolver` |
+| Detect `--absolute-git-dir` | Addressed | Query flag list at line 117 |
+| Detect `--git-dir` | Addressed | Query flag list at line 117 |
+| Detect `--show-toplevel` | Addressed | Query flag list at line 117 |
+| Detect `OpenRoot` | Addressed | Filesystem verb list at line 292 |
+| Scan production Go outside `cmd/entire/cli` | Addressed in implementation; test observes only a helper | Repository root at line 56 and walker at line 68 |
+| Avoid false positives for an unrelated `gitDir` parameter | Addressed | Object-aware bindings and negative control at line 226 |
+| Test `ResolveWorktreeMetadata("")` | Addressed through the real resolver | `metadata_test.go:227` |
+| Put the seven-of-seven strictness result in the PR description | Not addressed | Current PR description gives only a general fixture summary |
+
+## System Model
+
+### Read owner
+
+`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` owns interpretation of `.git`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree registration identity for the new repository-opening seam.
+
+### Guard owner
+
+`TestGitMetadataTraversalHasCanonicalOwner` owns enforcement of the temporary migration inventory. It scans production Go and rejects new metadata parsers, unapproved `.git` filesystem inspections, legacy resolver calls, and metadata-oriented `git rev-parse` queries.
+
+### Write and durable state
+
+This response performs no production writes and creates no durable state. The resolver reads filesystem metadata, while the guard reads and parses source files during tests.
+
+### Interruption and recovery
+
+Stopping during resolution or source scanning leaves no partial state, locks, temporary files, subprocesses, or goroutines. The operation can be retried directly after correcting the metadata or source violation.
+
+### Outermost outcome
+
+- An empty worktree root returns `worktree root is required` before CWD can influence resolution.
+- A registration symlink escaping `CommonDir/worktrees` is rejected by both `ResolveWorktreeMetadata` and `OpenPath`.
+- A forbidden metadata owner makes the guard test fail with a source position and remedy.
+
+## The Three Correctness Questions
+
+### Who owns the write?
+
+No component writes. `ResolveWorktreeMetadata` owns reads, and the guard test owns source-policy enforcement.
+
+### What survives interruption immediately before or after the operation?
+
+Nothing new. All affected operations are read-only and retry-safe.
+
+### Which test observes the real contract breaking on the old code?
+
+`TestResolveWorktreeMetadata_RequiresExplicitRoot` enters through the production resolver and would fail if the empty-root guard were removed.
+
+The guard’s current synthetic tests prove helper recognition, but they do not fully answer this question for cross-file constants or repository-wide scanning. That missing production-seam proof is the second medium finding.
+
+## Cleanup Proof
+
+No cleanup path is required because the change acquires no persistent resource and performs no mutation. The symlink-escape fixture calls `OpenPath` after the resolver failure and observes the same fail-closed result, showing that the earlier failure leaves no residual state that changes the next real operation.
+
+## Cleared Matrix Rows
+
+- Explicit empty root
+- Whitespace-only real directory
+- Normal checkout metadata
+- Symlink-aliased linked-worktree registration
+- Registration symlink escaping the common directory
+- Error propagation through `OpenPath`
+- Package-level string token recognition
+- Local string aliases
+- Rooted filesystem methods
+- Aliased legacy-resolver imports
+- Same-package legacy-resolver calls
+- Unrelated `gitDir` parameter negative control
+- Production source classification outside `cmd/entire/cli`
+- No production Git subprocess introduced
+- No durable write or interruption cleanup requirement
+
+## Verification
+
+The following checks passed on the uncommitted response:
+
+```text
+mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo -run '<review-response tests>' -count=1
+mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo -count=1
gofmt -d <three changed files>
git diff --check
+```
+
+The complete `mise run check` workflow was not rerun as part of this read-only correctness review.
+
+## Recommendation
+
+Keep the resolver changes. Before marking the review comment fully resolved:
+
+1. Make metadata-query exceptions flag-specific.
+2. Test the complete scanner against a temporary multi-file repository fixture.
+3. Restore the claimed `Readlink` positive control.
+4. Add the seven-of-seven versus three-of-seven result to the PR description.
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);
